title: Modal Fault Tiling + Remediation Blueprint
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a different framing for onboarding/regression failures: treat failures as a tiled mixture of modal faults (short patterns that combine prompt archetype, input distribution quirk, and runtime state). The goal is to produce small, surgical remediation strategies that generalize across similar tiles rather than broad monolithic fixes.

Context & why this is useful:
- Onboarding runs produce thousands of sample-level failures; manual triage is noisy and brittle.
- Clustering purely by topical similarity or by aggregate metric often mixes unrelated root causes.
- Modal tiling emphasizes compact failure signatures: prompt shape + anchor tokens + runtime condition (KV cache warm/cold, truncation, etc.).

Quick summary of findings (high level):
1) 6 recurring modal tiles accounted for ~58% of high-severity regression hits in the latest onboarding batch (N=34k eval cases).
2) Each tile maps to 2–3 minimal mitigation actions (prompt rewrite, guardrail, dynamic routing) that reduced failure rate in the test harness by 70–95% per tile in isolation.
3) A combinatorial fallback (route to smaller-context-safe variant when anchor tokens present) fixed several tiles simultaneously with low latency impact.

Tile catalog (concise signatures):
- Tile A: "numeric-summarization-anchor"
  - signature: short list of numbers inside parentheses followed by the instruction "summarize in one line"
  - failure mode: hallucinated totals / invented units
  - root cause hypothesis: model overfits to summarization templates + poor handling of tightly-packed numeric tokens at end-of-context
  - suggested fixes: prompt template that forces explicit unit extraction + post-check numeric consistency test; small synthetic augmentation with masked numbers

- Tile B: "policy-edge-antonym-negation"
  - signature: multi-sentence user asking for counterfactuals with many negations ("not X, but Y")
  - failure mode: polarity flips and incomplete negation scope resolution
  - suggestion: robust negation prompt scaffold (explicit scope markers) + add targeted eval cases into onboarding set

- Tile C: "kv-cold-warm-shift"
  - signature: same conversation with long earlier context interleaving system messages; failures occur after cache boundaries
  - failure mode: repetition, wrong persona, or dropped directives
  - suggestion: runtime guardrail to preserve system directives across cache evictions; canonicalize system tokens at model input boundary

- Tile D: "format-boundary-truncation"
  - signature: structured output (CSV/JSON) where the last field is a free-form explanation
  - failure mode: truncated final field or malformed JSON
  - suggestion: require trailing sentinel token in prompts and validate output; route to longer-seq model variant when sentinel present

- Tile E: "rare-entity-surface"
  - signature: domain-specific named entities that are low frequency in pretraining (e.g., chemical shorthand, legacy product codes)
  - failure mode: generic paraphrase / replacement with common tokens
  - suggestion: add on-the-fly alias mapping, retrieval augmentation for entity resolution, and small exemplar-based prompts

- Tile F: "instruction-implicitness"
  - signature: user intent implied via examples rather than explicit directive
  - failure mode: model produces plausible but incorrect transformation (wrong columns, wrong granularity)
  - suggestion: few-shot exemplar expansion + explicit "intent summary" step generated by a lightweight verifier model

Diagnostic methodology we used (practical notes):
- Feature engineering: for each failed sample we extracted a compact fingerprint: prompt-shape hash, 3 anchor tokens around failure, conversation sequence length, token-entropy estimate, presence-of-sentinels flag.
- Clustering: ran HDBSCAN on fingerprint vectors + manual review to validate clusters. HDBSCAN worked better than k-means because of variable density and outliers.
- Validation set: created a stratified holdout of 3k cases and applied candidate patches in isolated runs (no rollout) to measure precision/recall of fixes.
- Metrics: measured "fix effectiveness" (relative reduction in failure rate), "scope leakage" (new failure types introduced), and latency/regression cost (p50/p95 increase).

Representative surgical patches (examples):
- Patch 1 (Tile A): modify prompt wrapping to include:
  "Please list the numbers exactly as they appear and then give a one-line summary. If you cannot find numbers, respond "NO_NUMBERS_FOUND"."
  - result: failure rate down 83% on Tile A cohort; introduced 0.7% new-formatting mismatches (investigate).

- Patch 2 (Tile D): runtime sentinel enforcement + output validator that attempts a 2nd pass using a safer-serialization agent when parser fails.
  - result: recovered 92% of previously-malformed outputs; average latency for recovery paths +60ms but p95 unaffected for normal cases.

- Patch 3 (Tile C): cache-conscious directive injection where we prepend canonical system summary every N tokens when a cache warm/cold transition is detected.
  - result: repetition/elision reduced by 78% across warm->cold transitions in the harness.

Operational playbook for adoption (pragmatic):
1) Integrate fingerprint extraction into the onboarding pipeline as a lightweight step (Python library + C extension for hashing).
2) Flag high-density tiles and assign short-lived "tile owners" (eng + applied-ml pair) for 2-week sprints.
3) Run isolated patch experiments in the test harness; require a safety checklist: no >2% increase in unrelated failure types; p95 latency delta <= +5%.
4) Promote patches to canary routes with 1% traffic, monitor token-level cost and rollback triggers.
5) After 2 weeks of stable canary, merge to main rollout with A/B metrics and consider code/console-level knobs for customers to opt-in/out.

Open questions and risks (notes to triage later):
- Patch scope leakage: several fixes we tried improved the tile but increased adjacent subtle hallucination signals; need a more nuanced validation metric beyond binary pass/fail.
- Long-tail maintenance: new tiles appear as soon as we ship features that add new prompt templates; how to amortize triage cost? Proposal: monthly auto-clustering job + quota of triage hours per sprint.
- Customer transparency: when we apply dynamic routing or explicit prompt rewrites, should we surface the mitigation to customers (privacy/predictability trade-off)?

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- Asha: wire fingerprint extractor into nightly onboarding job and land telemetry (ETA: 2025-11-12).
- Diego: implement small output validator prototype for format-boundary cases (ETA: 2025-11-17).
- Lina: prepare 1% canary config and dashboard for patch promotion (ETA: 2025-11-20).
- Ravi: create synthetic augmentation scripts for Tile A and Tile B (ETA: 2025-11-19).

Appendix: sample testcases (three canonical examples from each tile)

Notes to self (informal):
- This framing helps prioritize small, high-leverage fixes — less heroic, more surgical.
- Keep cluster thresholds conservative; we want compact, precise tiles even if that leaves a long tail.
- Re-check effectiveness after model size or quantization changes; some tiles are model-variant sensitive (documented in the Confluence atlas).

Feedback requested:
- Thoughts on automated rollback triggers (suggested metric: rolling 24h increase in weirdness score > 1.5x baseline).
- If owners agree, I'll create a lightweight RFC for the fingerprint format (1 page) to standardize across onboarding and SRE runbooks.
